html:
Company: E-bikes producer · Home country: Japan · Size: Mid-sized (50-250 staff) · HS 871160 (Vehicles & transport equipment) · Generated 2026-11-21

1. Executive Summary

Verdict: ENTER WITH CAUTION. Real opportunity, but specific risks need a mitigation plan before scaling.

Market attractiveness: 6.0/10
Recommended entry mode: Exclusive distributor or agent, with a small local sales office

  • Import market of $3.31 m in 2024, growing 56.28% a year since 2019.
  • Supply is highly concentrated (HHI 2,568); top supplier India holds 34.04%.
  • CAGE distance from Japan: high.
  • EU-27 suppliers hold 4.59% of China's imports.

2. Market Size & Growth

Market size is measured as imports into China (UN Comtrade (China-reported imports, excluding re-imports of Chinese goods)). Imports show demand served from abroad, not total consumption.

Year Imports (USD)
2019 $355.32 k
2020 $7.83 m
2021 $10.34 m
2022 $3.86 m
2023 $2.79 m
2024 $3.31 m

CAGR 2019-2024: 56.28%.

HHI 2,568: Highly concentrated. A few suppliers dominate, so a newcomer must win share from incumbents or exploit buyers' wish to diversify supply (EU 'de-risking').

The EU-27's share of China's imports moved from 27.66% (2019) to 4.59% (2024).

4. PESTEL Analysis

  • Political: One-party state with active industrial policy (Made in China 2025, dual circulation). Geopolitical tension with the EU and US; retaliation risk in trade disputes (e.g. EU brandy, pork, dairy probes). Vehicles are a flashpoint in EU-China trade policy.
  • Economic: World's second-largest economy and a huge consumer market, but slower growth, weak consumer confidence and strong price competition from domestic champions. Latest: GDP growth 5.0% (2025), inflation 0.1% (World Bank).
  • Social: Digitally native consumers; 'guochao' preference for domestic brands among younger buyers; foreign brands win on safety, heritage and premium positioning.
  • Technological: World-leading e-commerce and super-apps (Tmall, JD, Douyin, WeChat); fast product cycles; strong domestic manufacturing capability.
  • Environmental: Dual-carbon goals (peak 2030, neutrality 2060) drive demand for clean-tech; growing ESG disclosure requirements. Electrification targets support EV and e-mobility demand.
  • Legal: Foreign Investment Law (2020) improved access; still complex licensing, local standards (GB/CCC), data-localisation rules and uneven IP enforcement.

5. CAGE Distance

Dimension Distance Evidence
Cultural High Different language families (Japonic vs Sinitic); localisation needed.
Administrative High Preferential access via RCEP. Large governance gap (WGI +1.37 vs -0.11).
Geographic Medium ~2,093 km between capitals.
Economic Medium GDP per capita $35,951 (home) vs $13,862 (target), ratio 2.6x.

Overall distance: High.

6. Tariffs, Trade Defence & Regulation

⚠️ Trade defence: EU anti-dumping and anti-subsidy duties on e-bikes from China have applied since 2019 (check the current rate and any expiry review).

  • CCC certification and MIIT product catalogue listing for vehicles; CCC for electric bicycles (GB 17761 standard)
  • Domestic producers dominate EVs and e-bikes; intense price competition
  • Customs registration of the consignee; Chinese-language labelling for retail goods
  • Foreign Investment Law (2020) and the Negative List: most sectors open to wholly foreign-owned enterprises (WFOE)
  • Data Security Law and Personal Information Protection Law (PIPL) for any customer data collected
  • Cross-border e-commerce (e.g. Tmall Global, JD Worldwide) allows testing demand under a lighter regime for many consumer goods

Verify current duties and requirements: - China Customs tariff and regulations (GACC) - MOFCOM trade remedy notices - EU Access2Markets: China export requirements - EU SME Centre (China market guides)

7. Risk Matrix

Risk Likelihood Impact Mitigation
Dominant incumbent supplier (India, 34.04% share) High High Differentiate on quality, service, sustainability and EU/China-specific certification rather than price.
Trade-defence or retaliation measures in the EU-China corridor High High Monitor trade-defence notices; diversify sourcing and production locations; build tariff scenarios into pricing.
Institutional and IP-protection risk Medium High Register trademarks and patents locally before entry; use contracts with local arbitration (e.g. CIETAC/HKIAC).
Brand and message mis-fit with local consumers Medium Medium Local consumer testing, native-language content, local marketplace and social channels.
Currency volatility (EUR/CNY/USD) Medium Medium Price in home currency where possible; hedge large contracts with forwards.

8. Recommended Entry Mode

Exclusive distributor or agent, with a small local sales office

  • Balances control and cost for a mid-attractiveness market.
  • A distributor brings market access; a sales office protects the brand and gathers market intelligence.
  • Inputs: attractiveness 6.0/10, CAGE distance high, institutional quality 4.8/10, company size mid-sized (50-250 staff).

9. Attractiveness Score Breakdown

Component Weight Score
Market size 25% 1.0/10
Growth 25% 10.0/10
Competitive openness 20% 7.4/10
Institutional quality 15% 4.8/10
Logistics 15% 6.8/10
Total 6.0/10

10. 90-Day Action Plan

  1. Days 1-30, validate: confirm the HS code and duty rate on official tariff tools, size the niche with customer interviews, shortlist 10 potential partners or channels in China.
  2. Days 1-30, compliance: map required certifications and labelling (see section 6), get quotes from a test lab or regulatory agent, register trademarks in the target market.
  3. Days 31-60, commercial model: build a landed-cost and pricing model (duties, freight, VAT, channel margins, FX), and draft the partner or channel agreement.
  4. Days 31-60, go-to-market: localise product pages, packaging and sales material; pick 1-2 launch channels consistent with the entry mode: exclusive distributor or agent, with a small local sales office.
  5. Days 61-90, pilot: ship a pilot order or open the online store, track sell-through, margin and customer feedback against go/no-go KPIs.
